$comment: Icon system config: the single place the icon set is decided. Semantic app name -> Phosphor icon name. Change a row and run `npm run icons:font` to regenerate the glyph map and the bundled font, the same way design/tokens.json drives the type system. Icons are Phosphor (https://phosphoricons.com, MIT), rendered as a FONT rather than SVG: react-native-svg is banned here (it throws synchronouslyUpdateUIProps inside Reanimated views and kills touch, RULE 5), and our Icon sits inside animated Pressables everywhere. A font glyph is plain <Text>: safe in Reanimated, tinted by `color`, scaled by `fontSize`. Amit's call, 2026-09-26: "completely shift to phosphor for every icon/glyph removing heroicons and lucide completely". Before that the app ran three faces at once (Heroicons outline, Heroicons solid, and a Lucide subset for the nine icons Heroicons had no twin for), which is the scatter that call ended. Phosphor has an equivalent for every one of those nine, so there is no fallback face any more: ONE font, assets/fonts/Phosphor.ttf. The SVGs come from the pinned `@phosphor-icons/core` devDependency, which is used only by scripts/gen-icons-font.mjs; nothing Phosphor ships at runtime except the font.
$outlineWeightNote: Every plain glyph name draws in this ONE Phosphor weight (scripts/gen-icons-font.mjs); `-fill` names and `active` entries stay FILL. Bold since 2026-10-10 (Amit, choosing from a Phosphor regular / Phosphor bold / Tabler comparison after "ours feel dull"): about 2.25px of stroke at 24dp against regular's 1.5px, with every Phosphor shape kept. Regular and bold are the only accepted values; mixing outline weights would be a second visual system inside one font.
$listWeightNote: The weight LIST ROWS draw their outline glyphs in (Icon `list`, used by the Settings row): regular, while standalone controls (bottom bar, chat header, composer) stay `outlineWeight` bold. Amit, 2026-10-11, on the S22 with 1.4.7: "settings icon seem too bold"; chose "bold chrome, regular rows" from a regular / bold / bold-at-20dp comparison. A column of bold glyphs reads heavy beside one line of text each; one bold glyph alone in a bar does not. Two weights, each with one job. Fills are the same in both.

glyphs.$comment: semantic name in the app -> Phosphor icon name (https://phosphoricons.com). A plain name is the top-level `outlineWeight`, BOLD since 2026-10-10 (node_modules/@phosphor-icons/core/assets/bold/<name>-bold.svg); a name ending `-fill` is the FILL weight (assets/fill/<name>.svg), for a mark that is always solid. Only one outline weight at a time, regular or bold: light/thin/duotone, or two outline weights, would be a second visual system inside one font. The generator fails on a name the package does not ship.
glyphs.$chevronNote: Phosphor calls the bare chevron a `caret`; its `chevron` does not exist. `caret-right` is the same open two-stroke angle Lucide's chevron-right was.
glyphs.$deviceNote: The Appearance screen's Color mode group mark, Bluesky's PhoneIcon (social-app AppearanceSettings.tsx): a handset DEVICE, not the call handset `call` draws.
glyphs.$appearanceNote: Bluesky's Settings row for Appearance draws a paint roller (social-app Settings.tsx, PaintRollerIcon).
glyphs.$aboutNote: Bluesky's Settings About row (CircleInfo) and the About screen's rows: Newspaper for each policy, Wrench for the version (social-app AboutSettings.tsx).
glyphs.$badgeCheckNote: The certified badge on a directory card (Amit, 2026-09-08: "certified icon should be like clarity"). The mark is the scalloped rosette with a check inside, which Clarity and Astrotalk both use; Phosphor's name for it is `seal-check`. Drawn as ONE glyph rather than as our own check inside an accent disc, which is what it was first built as: two shapes stacked to approximate a shape the icon set already had. FILLED since 2026-09-26 (Amit: "replace our seal check with phosphor seal check in blue colour, filled, with height equal to the first capital letter of the name"), so it is a `-fill` name rather than an `active` entry: the seal has no unselected state, the same reasoning as the category marks below. This reverses the earlier 'regular, like every other mark on the card' call; the category line now draws filled marks too, so the card has two solid marks rather than one odd one. Its one call site is ProviderRow, which sizes it to the name's cap height (VERIFIED_SEAL_SIZE).
glyphs.$callEndNote: Lucide's `phone-off` was the handset with a slash through it, and `phone-slash` is that same drawing. Phosphor also has `phone-disconnect` (the horizontal hang-up handset); it was NOT chosen because the decline/end controls were designed against the slashed mark and swapping the metaphor is a design decision, not a migration.
glyphs.speaker: speaker-high
glyphs.$downloadNote: `download-simple` (arrow into an open tray line) is Lucide's `download`; Phosphor's plain `download` is a closed box with an arrow, a heavier mark.
glyphs.$sendNote: `paper-plane-tilt` is the tilted plane Lucide's `send` drew. `paper-plane-right` is level, which reads as a different glyph in the composer.
glyphs.$deleteNote: `delete` is the composer's backspace key, not a bin: Lucide's `delete` was the backspace-key shape, and Phosphor names that shape `backspace`.
glyphs.$replyNote: Lucide's `reply` was an arrow pointing left with its tail bending back down on the right; Phosphor's `arrow-bend-up-left` is that drawing. Phosphor has no glyph called `reply`.
glyphs.$dotNote: Lucide's `circle` was an outline ring and so is Phosphor's regular `circle`; the pending-verification chip relies on it being a ring, not a solid dot.
glyphs.$stopNote: Phosphor has both `stop` and `square`; `stop` is the media-transport glyph and is what the recording control means. Lucide only had `square`.
glyphs.$unwindNote: Lucide's `sparkles` was one large four-point star with small ones beside it. Phosphor has no `sparkles`, but its `sparkle` (2.1.1) is the same composition: one large four-point star with two small plus-sparks. Closest available, and close.
glyphs.$categoryNote: The provider-type marks for the category line on a provider card (Listener / Astrologer). FILLED, which is why they are `-fill` names rather than `active` entries: they have no unselected state. Astrologer = filled moon-stars (owner decision 2026-09-26), `moon-stars-fill` over `sparkle-fill` because `unwind` is the sparkle. Listener = `butterfly-fill` since 2026-10-12 (Amit: the filled flower "looks like setting not flower"; its ring of petals reads as a gear at caption size), after `flower-fill` (2026-10-10) and `flower-lotus-fill` (2026-09-27) (Amit, on the S22: "we are not sales support, find something therapy vibe"). The headset it replaced read as a call-centre agent, which is the wrong promise for someone a member comes to in order to be heard; the lotus is the calm, therapeutic mark. `ear-fill` stays out for the original reason: `listen` already draws the ear in the onboarding word carousel, and `unwind` already owns the sparkle, so the lotus is also the one candidate that means nothing else in the set.
glyphs.$receiptNote: Billing-document glyph for the invoices settings row and inline bill/payment rows. Always drawn as fill in data rows (via `active` prop); the settings row uses the outline weight. Phosphor's `receipt` is the standard store-receipt shape.

$active: semantic name -> the FILL glyph `<Icon active>` renders for that name. Only where something renders the name active and the selected state genuinely fills: the member nav destinations in FloatingToolbar (home, heart, call, person) and the provider tab bar in ProviderHomeScreen (chat, heart, person) - Material 3's filled active nav icon, https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-bar/guidelines - plus the favourite heart, the rating star, and the TokenCounter wallet, which has passed `active` unconditionally since 2026-09-01 and so has always drawn the filled wallet. A name with no entry here renders its outline glyph in both states and colour carries `active`. Heroicons gave every icon a solid twin whether anything used it or not; this list is the ones something uses, so the font carries only glyphs that render. __tests__/iconSet.test.ts scans every `<Icon ... active>` call site and fails on a name missing from this map, because a missing fill does not error: it renders the outline glyph and the selected state silently becomes colour-only.
